CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LEARNING AREA - INTRODUCTION
Religion is the belief in and worship of God or gods. There are three types of religion in Nigeria - Christian, Muslim and Traditional religions.
RELIGIOUS BODIES IN NIGERIA
Religious bodies are the religious group of people with related common practices, faith and beliefs.
These bodies develop its members by teaching moral values.
EXAMPLES OF RELIGIOUS BODIES IN NIGERIA
1. Traditional Religious Bodies
Traditional religious bodies are the Sango worshippers, the Obatala worshippers, the Amadioha worshippers and the Olokun worshippers.
2. Christian Religious Bodies
Christian religious bodies are the Roman Catholic, the Church Missionary Society (CMS), the Baptist and the Pentecostal Movement, among others.
3. Islamic Religious Bodies
Islamic religious bodies are the Ansar-ud-deen, the Ahmadiyya and the Nawar-ud-deen sects, among others.
ROLES OF RELIGIOUS BODIES IN NATIONAL DEVELOPMENT
The roles of religious bodies Nigeria are -
1. Preaching of love and peace
2. Provision of education
3. Provision of health facilities and services
4. Encouragement of peaceful coexistence
5. Provision of social amenities such as roads, water, markets, etc.
6. Putting their members in check.
7. Interpret the law and order in Nigeria.
8. Teaching religion tolerance.

1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Explains the of religious bodies.
Pupil’s Activities - Listen to the teacher’s explanation.
3. Guides pupils to give examples of each religious bodies - Traditional, Christian and Muslim religious.
Pupil’s Activities - Give examples of each religious bodies - Traditional, Christian and Muslim religious.
4. Discusses the role of religious bodies in National Development.
Pupil’s Activities - Mention the role of religious bodies in National Development.
5. Summary the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.

To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.

topics.title: Religion and Religious Belief: Meaning and Types of Religion, Religious Intolerance and Problems of Religious Intolerance | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 11 Social Studies
topics.content:
RELIGION AND RELIGIOUS BELIEF: MEANING AND TYPES OF RELIGION, RELIGIOUS INTOLERANCE AND PROBLEMS OF RELIGIOUS INTOLERANCE
SOCIAL STUDIES
PRIMARY 5 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 11
THEME - NATIONAL VALUES EDUCATION
PREVIOUS LESSON - Modern Marriage: Main Features of Christian Marriage and Muslim Marriage, Values of Christian and Muslim Marriage and Marriage by Ordinance | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 10 Social Studies
TOPIC - RELIGION AND RELIGIOUS BELIEF
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Meaning and Types of Religion
3. Meaning of Religious Beliefs
4. Meaning, Causes and Problems of Religious Intolerance
5. Ways of Promoting Religious Tolerance
6. Values Related to Religious Tolerance
7. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
8. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of religion.
2. Explain the meaning of religious belief.
3. Mention three types of religion practised in Nigeria.
4. Explain the meaning of religious intolerance.
5. Mention at least five problems of religious intolerance.
6. State ways of promoting religious tolerance.
7. Mention values that promote religious tolerance, such as respect, tolerance, peace, love, understanding, cooperation, fairness, and kindness.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about modern marriage and the roles of religion in Christian and Muslim marriage.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by helping pupils understand religion, religious beliefs, different types of religion, religious intolerance, and the problems caused by religious intolerance.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Pictures of a church, mosque, and traditional worship setting
2. Charts showing different types of religion
3. Flashcards showing values such as respect, tolerance, and peace
4. Pictures showing people living and working together peacefully
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Religion is an important part of people’s lives. It influences the way people worship, behave, think, and relate with others.
People practise different religions and have different religious beliefs. In Nigeria, some of the major religions include Christianity, Islam, and Traditional African Religion.
Sometimes, people may fail to respect the beliefs of others. This is called religious intolerance. Religious intolerance can cause conflict, discrimination, hatred, division, and loss of lives and property.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about the meaning and types of religion, religious intolerance, the problems of religious intolerance, and the importance of respect, tolerance, peace, love, understanding, cooperation, fairness, and kindness.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF RELIGION
Religion is a system of beliefs and practices through which people relate to and worship God or a higher power.
Religion can influence people’s beliefs, values, behaviour, customs, and way of life.
MEANING OF RELIGIOUS BELIEF
Religious belief is what a person or group accepts as true about God, worship, faith, and spiritual matters.
People may have different religious beliefs, and these beliefs should be treated with respect and tolerance.
TYPES OF RELIGION
Some major religions practised in Nigeria include:
1. Christianity - Christianity is based on the teachings of Jesus Christ. Christians worship in churches and use the Bible as their holy book.
2. Islam - Islam is based on the teachings of Prophet Muhammad. Muslims worship in mosques and use the Qur’an as their holy book.
3. Traditional African Religion - Traditional African religion refers to the indigenous religious beliefs and practices of African communities. These practices vary from one community to another.
LESSON 2 - RELIGIOUS INTOLERANCE
Religious intolerance is the refusal to respect or accept people who have different religious beliefs.
For example, insulting someone because of their religion, preventing people from practising their religion peacefully, or treating people unfairly because of their faith are forms of religious intolerance.
CAUSES OF RELIGIOUS INTOLERANCE
Religious intolerance may be caused by:
1. Lack of understanding of other religions.
2. Prejudice and discrimination.
3. False information about other religions.
4. Hatred and fear.
5. Lack of respect for other people’s beliefs.
6. Poor upbringing and negative influence.
7. Misinterpretation of religious teachings.
PROBLEMS OF RELIGIOUS INTOLERANCE
Religious intolerance can lead to:
1. Conflict - People may disagree and fight because of religious differences.
2. Discrimination - People may be treated unfairly because of their religion.
3. Loss of lives and property - Serious religious conflicts can cause deaths and destruction.
4. Fear and insecurity - People may become afraid to live or worship freely.
5. Division - It can separate families, communities, and groups.
6. Hatred - It can create hatred between people of different faiths.
7. Slow development - Conflict can prevent communities from developing peacefully.
LESSON 3 - WAYS OF PROMOTING RELIGIOUS TOLERANCE
Religious tolerance means respecting and accepting people who have different religious beliefs from ours.
Religious tolerance can be promoted by:
1. Respecting other people’s religious beliefs.
2. Living peacefully with people of different religions.
3. Avoiding insults and discrimination.
4. Learning about other religions respectfully.
5. Promoting dialogue and understanding.
6. Obeying laws that protect people’s rights.
7. Teaching children to respect people who are different from them.
8. Solving disagreements peacefully.
VALUES RELATED TO RELIGIOUS TOLERANCE
Important values include:
1. Respect - Treating people and their beliefs with dignity.
2. Tolerance - Accepting that people may have different beliefs.
3. Peace - Living together without fighting or violence.
4. Love - Caring for and treating others well.
5. Understanding - Trying to learn and understand other people’s beliefs.
6. Cooperation - Working together peacefully with others.
7. Fairness - Treating everyone equally and justly.
8. Kindness - Being helpful and caring towards others.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. Religion is a system of beliefs and practices through which people ______.
A. build houses
B. play games
C. sell goods
D. worship God or a higher power
2. Which of the following is a major religion practised in Nigeria?
A. Christianity
B. Football
C. Farming
D. Trading
3. Christians use the ______ as their holy book.
A. Bible
B. Qur’an
C. Newspaper
D. Dictionary
4. Religious intolerance means ______.
A. living peacefully with others
B. respecting other religions
C. refusing to respect people with different beliefs
D. helping people of different religions
5. Which of the following promotes religious tolerance?
A. Hatred
B. Respect
C. Discrimination
D. Violence
B. Fill in the Gaps
6. Christianity, Islam, and Traditional African Religion are types of ______.
7. Muslims use the ______ as their holy book.
8. Refusing to respect people with different religious beliefs is called religious ______.
9. Religious intolerance can cause conflict and ______.
20. Treating everyone equally is called ______.
C. True or False
11. People can have different religious beliefs. ______
12. Religious intolerance promotes peace. ______
13. Respect for other people’s beliefs promotes peaceful living. ______
14. Religious intolerance can lead to conflict and division. ______
15. People should be discriminated against because of their religion. ______
D. Matching
16. Christianity - A. Refusing to respect different beliefs
17. Islam - B. Treating people equally
18. Religious Intolerance - C. Religion based on the teachings of Jesus Christ
19. Fairness - D. Religion based on the teachings of Islam
20. Tolerance - E. Accepting and respecting different beliefs
ANSWER KEY
1. D 2. A 3. A 4. C 5. B
6. religion
7. Qur’an
8. intolerance
9. division
10. fairness
11. True
12. False
13. True
14. True
15. False
16. C - Religion based on the teachings of Jesus Christ
17. D - Religion based on the teachings of Islam
18. A - Refusing to respect different beliefs
19. B - Treating people equally
20. E - Accepting and respecting different beliefs
SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that religion is a system of beliefs and practices through which people worship God or a higher power. They also learned that religious belief refers to what people accept as true about God, worship, and spiritual matters.
Pupils learned about three major types of religion practised in Nigeria: Christianity, Islam, and Traditional African Religion.
They also learned that religious intolerance means refusing to respect or accept people who have different religious beliefs. Religious intolerance can cause conflict, discrimination, hatred, division, fear, and loss of lives and property.
Pupils learned that religious tolerance can be promoted through respect, tolerance, peace, love, understanding, cooperation, fairness, and kindness.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher asks pupils:
- What is religion?
- Which religions do you know?p
- Where do Christians worship?
- Where do Muslims worship?
- Do all people have the same religious beliefs?
The teacher explains that people have different religious beliefs and practices. People should respect one another even when their religions are different.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions and mention religions they know.
Step 2: Meaning of Religion
The teacher explains that religion is a system of beliefs and practices through which people worship God or a higher power.
- Religion can influence people’s behaviour, values, customs, and way of life.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils repeat the meaning of religion and give examples of religious practices.
Step 3: Meaning of Religious Belief
The teacher explains that religious belief is what a person or group accepts as true about God, worship, and spiritual matters.
- People may have different religious beliefs, and these beliefs should be respected.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain what they understand by religious belief.
Step 4: Types of Religion
The teacher explains three major types of religion practised in Nigeria:
- Christianity - Based on the teachings of Jesus Christ. Christians worship in churches and use the Bible.
- Islam - Based on the teachings of Prophet Muhammad. Muslims worship in mosques and use the Qur’an.
- Traditional African Religion - Refers to the traditional religious beliefs and practices of African communities.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention the three types of religion and identify their places of worship or holy books where applicable.
Step 5: Meaning of Religious Intolerance
The teacher explains that religious intolerance is refusing to respect or accept people who have different religious beliefs.
Examples include:
- Insulting people because of their religion.
- Treating people unfairly because of their beliefs.
- Preventing others from peacefully practising their religion.
- Fighting because of religious differences.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils give examples of respectful and disrespectful behaviour towards people of other religions.
Step 6: Problems of Religious Intolerance
The teacher explains that religious intolerance can cause:
- Conflict - People may fight because of religious differences.
- Discrimination - People may be treated unfairly because of their religion.
- Hatred - It can create hatred among different religious groups.
- Division - It can separate families and communities.
- Fear and insecurity - People may feel unsafe.
- Loss of lives and property - Serious conflicts can cause deaths and destruction.
- Slow development - Conflict can prevent communities from developing peacefully.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention some problems caused by religious intolerance.
Step 7: Ways of Promoting Religious Tolerance
The teacher explains that religious tolerance can be promoted by:
- Respecting other people’s beliefs.
- Living peacefully with people of different religions.
- Avoiding insults and discrimination.
- Learning about other religions respectfully.
- Solving disagreements peacefully.
- Promoting dialogue and understanding.
- Treating everyone fairly.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils suggest ways they can live peacefully with people of different religions.
Step 8: Values That Promote Religious Tolerance
The teacher explains the following values:
- Respect - Treating people and their beliefs with dignity.
- Tolerance - Accepting that people may have different beliefs.
- Peace - Living together without fighting.
- Love - Caring for others.
- Understanding - Trying to understand other people’s beliefs.
- Cooperation - Working together peacefully.
- Fairness - Treating everyone equally.
- Kindness - Being helpful and caring towards others.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain how these values can promote peaceful living.
Step 9: Group Activity
The teacher divides the pupils into groups.
- Group 1: Mention three types of religion.
- Group 2: State five problems of religious intolerance.
- Group 3: State five ways of promoting religious tolerance.
- Group 4: Mention eight values that promote religious tolerance.
Each group presents its answers to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write, and present their answers.
Step 10: Lesson Summary
The teacher reviews the meaning of religion and religious belief, types of religion, religious intolerance, its problems, and values that promote religious tolerance.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 11: Evaluation
The teacher gives pupils the 20-question practice exercise.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils complete the Multiple Choice, Fill in the Gaps, True or False, and Matching questions.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Leadership: Who is a Leader, Types of Leadership, Selection of Leaders, Functions of Political Leaders, Formation and Changes of Political Parties and Attributes of Good and Bad Leadership | Primary 5 (Basic 5) Second Term Week 1 Social Studies
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils to,
1. Explain the meaning of religion.
2. Explain the meaning of religious belief.
3. Mention three types of religion practised in Nigeria.
4. State the holy books associated with Christianity and Islam.
5. Explain the meaning of religious intolerance.
6. Mention at least five problems of religious intolerance.
7. State at least five ways of promoting religious tolerance.
8. Mention at least five values that promote religious tolerance.
9. Explain why people should respect other people’s religious beliefs.

topics.title: Problems of Parenthood: STIs, STDs and HIV/AIDS, Their Effects, Responsible Sexual Behaviour and Relevant Values | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 8 Social Studies
topics.content:
PROBLEMS OF PARENTHOOD: STIs, STDs AND HIV/AIDs, THEIR EFFECTS, RESPONSIBLE AND RELEVANT VALUES
SOCIAL STUDIES
PRIMARY 5 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 8
THEME - NATIONAL VALUES EDUCATION
PREVIOUS LESSON - Responsible Parenthood: Who Are Parents, Duties of Parents and Characteristics of Responsible Parenthood | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 6 Social Studies
TOPIC - PROBLEMS OF PARENTHOOD
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Meaning and Effects of STIs, STDs and HIV/AIDs
3. Responsible Sexual Behaviour
4. Values Relevant to Prevent STIs, STDs and HIV/AIDs
5. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
7. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of STIs and STDs.
2. State the meaning of HIV and AIDS.
3. Mention some examples of STIs and STDs.
4. Identify some effects of STIs, STDs, and HIV/AIDS.
5. Explain what responsible sexual behaviour means.
6. Mention ways children can protect themselves from sexual abuse and risky behaviour.
7. Identify values such as self-control, respect, honesty, responsibility, and discipline that promote healthy behaviour.
8. Explain why people living with HIV/AIDS should not be discriminated against.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about responsible parenthood, the duties of parents, and the characteristics of responsible parents.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by helping pupils understand some health and social problems that can affect individuals and families, as well as the importance of responsible behaviour, personal safety, and seeking help from trusted adults.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Charts showing personal safety and healthy behaviours
2. Pictures illustrating healthy living
3. Flashcards showing STI, STD, HIV, and AIDS
4. Posters on HIV/AIDS awareness
5. Age-appropriate educational video, where available
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Good health and safety are important to everyone. Some infections can be passed from one person to another through sexual contact. These infections are called sexually transmitted infections (STIs) or sexually transmitted diseases (STDs).
One important infection is HIV, which can weaken the body’s ability to fight diseases. Children need to learn how to protect themselves by making safe and responsible choices, respecting personal boundaries, and telling a trusted adult when they feel unsafe or experience inappropriate behaviour.
People living with HIV or other illnesses should be treated with kindness and respect, not discrimination.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about STIs, STDs, HIV/AIDS, their effects, responsible sexual behaviour, and the values that promote health and personal safety.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF STIs AND STDs
STI means Sexually Transmitted Infection. It refers to an infection that can be passed from one person to another through sexual contact.
STD means Sexually Transmitted Disease. It refers to a disease that results from certain sexually transmitted infections.
Examples include gonorrhoea, syphilis, chlamydia, and HIV infection.
For Primary 5 pupils, the emphasis should be on personal safety, avoiding risky sexual behaviour, seeking help from trusted adults, and obtaining proper medical care.
HIV/AIDS
HIV means Human Immunodeficiency Virus. It attacks the body’s immune system and can make it difficult for the body to fight infections.
AIDS means Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome. It is the advanced stage of HIV infection when the immune system has been severely weakened.
HIV can be prevented, and people living with HIV can receive treatment and live healthy lives.
LESSON 2 - EFFECTS OF STIs, STDs AND HIV/AIDs
These infections can have serious effects if they are not prevented or properly treated. They may cause:
1. Poor health and weakness.
2. Pain and discomfort.
3. Difficulty in carrying out daily activities.
4. Emotional stress and worry.
5. Problems with future health.
6. Stigma and discrimination.
7. Serious illness when left untreated.
Children should understand that a person should never be mocked or discriminated against because of an illness or HIV status.
RESPONSIBLE SEXUAL BEHAVIOUR
Responsible sexual behaviour means making safe, respectful, and age-appropriate choices concerning one’s body and relationships.
For Primary 5 pupils, responsible behaviour includes:
1. Avoiding sexual activity and recognising that children are not ready for sexual relationships.
2. Protecting personal boundaries and saying “No” when uncomfortable with inappropriate touching or behaviour.
3. Avoiding risky situations and people who pressure them into inappropriate activities.
4. Reporting sexual abuse or unwanted sexual behaviour to a trusted adult.
5. Seeking help from parents, guardians, teachers, healthcare professionals, or other trusted adults when concerned about health or safety.
6. Avoiding sharing personal or intimate images with others.
7. Respecting other people’s bodies and personal boundaries.
LESSON 3 - VALUES RELEVANT TO PREVENTING STIs, STDs AND HIV/AIDs
Important values include:
1. Self-control - Being able to make safe and responsible choices.
2. Respect - Respecting one’s body and the boundaries of others.
3. Honesty - Telling the truth and seeking help when necessary.
4. Responsibility - Taking care of one’s health and safety.
5. Discipline - Avoiding harmful or risky behaviour.
6. Courage - Speaking up when something is wrong.
7. Kindness - Treating people living with HIV or other illnesses with care and respect.
8. Seeking help - Telling a trusted  adult when faced with danger or abuse.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. STI means ______.
A. Special Teaching Instruction
B. Social Training Institution
C. School Treatment Information
D. Sexually Transmitted Infection
2. HIV means ______.
A. Health Information Virus
B. Human Infection Vaccine
C. Human Immunodeficiency Virus
D. Human Immune Vaccine
3. Which of the following is an example of an STI/STD?
A. Malaria
B. Gonorrhoea
C. Measles
D. Common cold
4. Which value helps a person make safe and responsible choices?
A. Self-control
B. Dishonesty
C. Violence
D. Carelessness
5. What should a child do when faced with inappropriate sexual behaviour?
A. Run away without telling anyone
B. Keep it secret
C. Blame themselves
D. Tell a trusted adult
B. Fill in the Gaps
6. ______ is a virus that attacks the body’s immune system.
7. Children should show ______ for their bodies and the boundaries of others.
8. ______ helps people make safe and responsible choices.
9. Children should tell a ______ adult when they feel unsafe.
10. ______ means being truthful and telling the truth.
C. True or False
11. HIV can affect the body’s immune system. ______
12. Children should report inappropriate sexual behaviour to a trusted adult. ______
13. People living with HIV should be discriminated against. ______
14. Self-control is an important value for making responsible choices. ______
15. STIs and STDs can affect people’s health. ______
D. Matching
16. STI - A. Being truthful
17. HIV - B. Virus that attacks the immune system
18. Self-control - C. Sexually Transmitted Infection
19. Honesty - D. Making safe and responsible choices
20. Respect - E. Treating oneself and others with dignity
ANSWER KEY
1. D 2. C. 3. B. 4. A 5. D
6. HIV
7. respect
8. self-control
9. trusted
10. honesty
11. True
12. True
13. False
14. True
15. True
16. C - Sexually Transmitted Infection
17. B - Virus that attacks the immune system
18. D - Making safe and responsible choices
19. A - Being truthful
20. E - Treating oneself and others with dignity
SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that STIs are sexually transmitted infections, while STDs are diseases that can result from sexually transmitted infections. They also learned that HIV is a virus that attacks the body’s immune system and that AIDS is the advanced stage of HIV infection.
Pupils learned that STIs, STDs, and HIV/AIDS can affect a person’s health, emotions, and family life if not properly prevented or treated.
They also learned about responsible behaviour, such as respecting personal boundaries, avoiding risky situations, reporting inappropriate sexual behaviour, and seeking help from trusted adults.
Important values include self-control, respect, honesty, responsibility, discipline, courage, and kindness. Pupils also learned that people living with HIV/AIDS should be treated with respect and kindness and should not be discriminated against.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher asks pupils:
- What does it mean to be healthy?
- How can we protect ourselves from harmful situations?
- Who can we tell when we feel unsafe?
The teacher explains that some health and safety problems can affect individuals and families. Children need to know how to make safe choices and seek help when necessary.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions and mention trusted adults they can talk to.
Step 2: Meaning of STI and STD
The teacher explains that STI means Sexually Transmitted Infection. It is an infection that can be passed from one person to another through sexual contact.
- STD means Sexually Transmitted Disease. It refers to a disease resulting from certain sexually transmitted infections.
Examples include gonorrhoea, syphilis, and chlamydia.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils repeat the meanings of STI and STD and mention examples.
Step 3: Meaning of HIV and AIDS
The teacher explains that HIV means Human Immunodeficiency Virus. It attacks the body’s immune system.
- AIDS means Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome. It can occur at an advanced stage of HIV infection when the immune system has been seriously weakened.
The teacher explains that people living with HIV can receive medical treatment and should not be discriminated against.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils state the full meanings of HIV and AIDS.
Step 4: Effects of STIs, STDs and HIV/AIDS
The teacher explains that these infections can affect a person’s health and wellbeing.
Possible effects include:
- Poor health
- Weakness
- Pain and discomfort
- Emotional stress
- Serious illness when not properly treated
- Stigma and discrimination
The teacher explains that people with these conditions should seek appropriate medical care.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention some possible effects.
Step 5: Responsible Behaviour
The teacher explains that responsible behaviour means making safe, respectful, and age-appropriate choices.
For children, responsible behaviour includes:
- Avoiding sexual activity.
- Respecting personal boundaries.
- Saying “No” to inappropriate touching.
- Avoiding people or situations that make them feel unsafe.
- Not sharing private or intimate pictures.
Telling a trusted adult when something is wrong.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss safe ways of responding to uncomfortable situations.
Step 6: Reporting Sexual Abuse
The teacher explains that children should not keep sexual abuse or inappropriate sexual behaviour secret.
- If someone touches them inappropriately, pressures them, or makes them feel unsafe, they should tell a parent, guardian, teacher, or another trusted adult.
The teacher emphasises that the child is not to blame for abuse.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify trusted adults they can report to.
Step 7: Values Relevant to Responsible Behaviour
The teacher explains the following values:
- Self-control - Making safe choices and avoiding harmful behaviour.
- Respect - Respecting one’s body and the bodies of others.
- Honesty - Telling the truth and seeking help when necessary.
- Responsibility - Taking care of one’s health and safety.
- Discipline - Following good rules and avoiding risky behaviour.
- Courage - Speaking up when something is wrong.
- Kindness - Treating people living with HIV or other illnesses with care.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain how these values can help them stay safe.
Step 8: Preventing Stigma and Discrimination
The teacher explains that HIV/AIDS is a health condition. People living with HIV should not be mocked, rejected, or discriminated against.
- Everyone should show them kindness, respect, and support.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils state how they should treat someone living with HIV.
Step 9: Group Activity
The teacher divides the pupils into groups.
- Group 1: State the meanings of STI, STD, HIV, and AIDS.
- Group 2: List four possible effects of STIs, STDs, and HIV/AIDS.
- Group 3: List five responsible behaviours that help children stay safe.
- Group 4: List five values that promote responsible behaviour.
Each group presents its work to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write, and present their answers.
Step 10: Lesson Summary
The teacher reviews the meaning of STIs, STDs, HIV/AIDS, their effects, responsible behaviour, personal safety, and relevant values.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 11: Evaluation
The teacher gives pupils the 20-question practice exercise.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils complete the Multiple Choice, Fill in the Gaps, True or False, and Matching questions.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Traditional Marriage: Meaning of Traditional Marriage, Modern Marriage, Main Features and Values of Traditional Marriage | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 9 Social Studies
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils to,
1. Explain the meaning of STI and STD.
2. State the full meanings of HIV and AIDS.
3. Mention at least three examples of STIs or STDs.
4. State at least three effects of STIs, STDs, and HIV/AIDS.
5. Explain the meaning of responsible behaviour.
6. Mention at least four ways children can protect themselves from inappropriate sexual behaviour.
7. Mention at least five values that promote responsible behaviour.
8. Explain why people living with HIV/AIDS should be treated with respect and not discriminated against.

topics.title: Responsible Parenthood: Who Are Parents, Duties of Parents and Characteristics of Responsible Parenthood | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 6 Social Studies
topics.content:
RESPONSIBE PARENTHOOD: WHO ARE PARENTS, DUTIES OF PARTS AND CHARACTERISTICS OF RESPONSIBE PARENTHOOD
SOCIAL STUDIES
PRIMARY 5 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 6
THEME - NATIONAL VALUES EDUCATION
PREVIOUS LESSON - Roles Played by Families: Consequences, Roles of Families in Providing Useful Advice and Unhealthy Marriage Practices | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 5 Social Studies
TOPIC - RESPONSIBE PARENTHOOD
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Who are Parents?
3. Duties of Parents
4. Meaning, Characteristics and importance of Responsible Parenthood
5. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
6. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain who parents are.
2. Mention at least six duties of parents.
3. Explain the meaning of responsible parenthood.
4. Identify at least six characteristics of responsible parenthood.
5. Explain the importance of parents providing care, protection, education, and guidance.
6. State how responsible parenthood helps to promote a happy and peaceful family.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about the roles played by families, the importance of useful advice, and healthy and unhealthy marriage practices.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by helping pupils understand who parents are, their duties towards their children, and the qualities of responsible parents.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Pictures of parents caring for their children
2. Pictures of parents providing food, clothing, and shelter
3. Pictures of parents helping children with schoolwork
4. Charts showing the duties of parents
5. Flashcards showing characteristics of responsible parenthood
6. Short video clips showing responsible parenting, where available
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Parents are important members of the family. They care for, protect, guide, and support their children.
Parents provide basic needs such as food, clothing, shelter, education, and healthcare. They also teach children good behaviour and values such as respect, honesty, kindness, and responsibility.
Responsible parenthood means taking good care of children and performing parental duties properly. Responsible parents show love, provide guidance, protect their children, support their education, and help them grow into responsible members of society.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about who parents are, the duties of parents, and the characteristics of responsible parenthood.
LESSON 1 - WHO ARE PARENTS?
Parents are the adults who care for, guide, protect, and support their children. They may be a child’s mother, father, or legal guardian.
Parents have an important role in helping children grow into responsible and useful members of society.
DUTIES OF PARENTS
Parents have many duties towards their children, including:
1. Providing basic needs - They provide food, clothing, shelter, and other necessities.
2. Providing education - They support children’s education and provide necessary learning materials.
3. Providing healthcare - They ensure that children receive appropriate medical care when needed.
4. Protection - They protect children from danger, abuse, and harmful situations.
5. Guidance and discipline - They teach children good behaviour and correct them appropriately.
6. Providing love and care - They show children affection, encouragement, and emotional support.
7. Teaching good values - They teach honesty, respect, kindness, responsibility, and hard work.
8. Providing a safe home - They create a safe and supportive environment for children.
9. Preparing children for adulthood - They help children develop useful skills and make responsible choices.
LESSON 2 - MEANING OF RESPONSIBLE PARENTHOOD
Responsible parenthood means performing the duties of caring for, protecting, guiding, and supporting children properly and making responsible decisions for the wellbeing of the family.
Responsible parents consider the needs, safety, education, health, and future development of their children.
CHARACTERISTICS OF RESPONSIBLE PARENTHOOD
A responsible parent should demonstrate the following qualities:
1. Love and Care - Responsible parents show genuine love, care, and concern for their children.
2. Responsibility - They take their duties towards their children seriously.
3. Patience - They remain patient when teaching and correcting their children.
4. Good Communication - They listen to their children and communicate with them respectfully.
5. Protection - They take reasonable steps to keep their children safe from harm.
6. Good Example - They demonstrate good behaviour because children often learn by observing adults.
7. Support for Education - They encourage children to learn and take their education seriously.
8. Provision of Basic Needs - They make reasonable efforts to provide food, clothing, shelter, healthcare, and other essential needs.
9. Proper Guidance - They help children make good decisions and avoid harmful behaviour.
10. Fairness - They treat their children fairly and avoid unnecessary discrimination among them.
LESSON 3 - IMPORTANCE OF RESPONSIBLE PARENTHOOD
Responsible parenthood helps to:
1. Promote peaceful family life.
2. Raise well-behaved and responsible children.
3. Provide children with proper guidance.
4. Improve children’s educational development.
5. Protect children from harm.
6. Build strong family relationships.
7. Prepare children to become responsible members of society.
8. Promote love, unity, and cooperation in the family.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. Parents are adults who ______.
A. care for and guide their children
B. refuse to help their children
C. avoid their family duties
D. teach children bad behaviour
2. Which of the following is a duty of parents?
A. Neglecting children
B. Encouraging children to fight
C. Preventing children from learning
D. Providing basic needs
3. Which of the following is a basic need that parents should provide?
A. Food
B. Toys only
C. Television games
D. Expensive phones
4. Responsible parenthood means ______.
A. refusing to educate children
B. neglecting children
C. properly caring for and guiding children
D. allowing children to do anything they want
5. Which of the following is a characteristic of responsible parenthood?
A. Neglect
B. Dishonesty
C. Patience
D. Violence
B. Fill in the Gaps
Use the following words to complete the sentences: education, love, protection, parents, responsibility
6. ______ are adults who care for and guide their children.
7. Parents should provide ______ for their children’s safety.
8. Parents should support their children’s ______.
9. Responsible parents show ______ and care to their children.
10. Responsible parenthood requires ______.
C. True or False
11. Parents have a responsibility to care for their children. ______
12. Responsible parents should provide guidance to their children. ______
13. Parents should encourage children to behave dishonestly. ______
14. Education is one of the responsibilities of parents. ______
15. Responsible parenthood promotes hatred among family members. ______
D. Matching
16. Love and care - A. Helping children learn
17. Responsible Parenthood - B. Adults who care for and guide children
18. Protection - C. Keeping children safe
19. Parents - D. Showing affection and concern
20. Education - E. Proper care, guidance, and support of children
ANSWER KEY
1. A 2. D 3. A 4. B 5. C
6. parents
7. protection
8. education
9. love
10. responsibility
11. True
12. True
13. False
14. True
15. False
16. Love and care - D. Showing affection and concern
17. Responsible Parenthood - E. Proper care, guidance, and support of children
18. Protection - C. Keeping children safe
19. Parents - B. Adults who care for and guide children
20. Education - A. Helping children learn
SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that parents are adults who care for, guide, protect, and support their children.
They learned that the duties of parents include providing food, clothing, shelter, education, healthcare, protection, love, care, guidance, and discipline.
Pupils also learned that responsible parenthood means taking proper care of children and performing parental duties responsibly. The characteristics of responsible parents include love, patience, responsibility, good communication, protection, fairness, good example, and proper guidance.
Responsible parenthood helps to promote peace, unity, good behaviour, strong family relationships, and the proper development of children.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher displays pictures of parents caring for, teaching, feeding, and protecting their children.
The teacher asks:
- Who are the people in the pictures?
- What are they doing for the children?
- What do your parents or guardians do for you?
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the pictures and answer the questions.
Step 2: Who Are Parents?
The teacher explains that parents are adults who care for, guide, protect, and support their children.
- Parents may be a child’s mother, father, or guardian.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention the people who care for and guide them at home.
Step 3: Duties of Parents
The teacher explains that parents have many duties towards their children. These include:
- Providing food.
- Providing clothing and shelter.
- Paying for or supporting education.
- Providing healthcare.
- Protecting children from danger.
- Providing love and care.
- Teaching good behaviour.
- Giving guidance and appropriate discipline.
- Supporting children’s development.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention the duties their parents or guardians perform at home.
Step 4: Meaning of Responsible Parenthood
The teacher explains that responsible parenthood means taking proper care of children and performing parental duties responsibly.
- Responsible parents consider the health, safety, education, needs, and future development of their children.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain what they understand by responsible parenthood.
Step 5: Characteristics of Responsible Parenthood
The teacher explains the characteristics of responsible parents:
- Love and care - They show affection and concern for their children.
- Responsibility - They take their duties seriously.
- Patience - They remain calm when teaching and correcting children.
- Good communication - They listen and speak respectfully with their children.
- Protection - They take reasonable steps to keep children safe.
- Good example - They demonstrate good behaviour for children to follow.
- Fairness - They treat children fairly.
- Proper guidance - They help children make good decisions.
- Support for education - They encourage children to learn and do well in school.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify characteristics of responsible parents from examples given by the teacher.
Step 6: Importance of Responsible Parenthood
The teacher explains that responsible parenthood:
- Promotes peace in the family.
- Helps children develop good behaviour.
- Provides children with proper guidance.
- Protects children from harm.
- Supports children’s education.
- Builds strong family relationships.
- Promotes love and unity.
- Helps children become responsible members of society.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils state the benefits of responsible parenthood.
Step 7: Examples of Responsible Parenting
The teacher gives examples:
- A parent ensures that a child attends school.
- A parent takes a sick child to a health facility.
- A parent teaches a child to respect others.
- A parent listens to a child’s concerns.
- A parent protects a child from dangerous situations.
- A parent provides guidance when the child has a problem.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils give other examples of responsible parenting.
Step 8: Group Activity
The teacher divides the pupils into groups.
- Group 1: List six duties of parents.
- Group 2: List six characteristics of responsible parenthood.
- Group 3: State five benefits of responsible parenthood.
- Group 4: Explain how parents can help children become responsible members of society.
Each group presents its work to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write, and present their answers.
Step 9: Lesson Summary
The teacher reviews who parents are, the duties of parents, the meaning of responsible parenthood, and its characteristics and importance.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 10: Evaluation
The teacher gives pupils the 20-question practice exercise.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils complete the Multiple Choice, Fill in the Gaps, True or False, and Matching questions.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Primary 5 - Social Studies Mid Term Test Questions and Answers
Problems of Parenthood: STIs, STDs and HIV/AIDS, Their Effects, Responsible Sexual Behaviour and Relevant Values | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 8 Social Studies
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils to,
1. Explain who parents are.
2. Mention at least six duties of parents.
3. Define responsible parenthood.
4. Mention at least six characteristics of responsible parenthood.
5. Explain why parents should provide education, protection, healthcare, and basic needs.
6. State at least four benefits of responsible parenthood.
7. Explain how responsible parents help children become responsible members of society.

topics.title: Other People in the Family: Other Family Members, Their Relationship to Us and Obligations of Family Members | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 1 Social Studies
topics.content:
OTHER PEOPLE IN THE FAMILY: OTHER FAMILY MEMBERS, THEIR RELATIONSHIP TO US AND OBLIGATIONS OF THE FAMILY MEMBERS
SOCIAL STUDIES
PRIMARY 5 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 1
THEME - NATIONAL VALUES EDUCATION
PREVIOUS LESSON - Security Agencies and Their Primary Duties: Meaning of Security, Security Agents in Nigeria and Their Duties | Primary 4 (Basic 4) Third Term Week 10 Social Studies
TOPIC - OTHER PEOPLE IN THE FAMILY
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Meaning of Family Members
3. Other Family Members and Their Relationships
4. Obligations of Family Members, Parents and Guardians, Children and Other Family Members
5. Importance of Family Obligations
6. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
7. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of family members.
2. Identify other people in the family apart from parents and children.
3. State the relationship between grandparents, uncles, aunts, cousins, nephews, and nieces and themselves.
4. Explain the obligations of different family members.
5. Mention at least five duties of children towards their family.
6. Explain the importance of love, respect, cooperation, and responsibility among family members.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about the family, types of family, and immediate family members, such as the father, mother, brothers, and sisters.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by introducing pupils to other members of the family, their relationships with one another, and the obligations of family members.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Pictures of different family members
2. Family tree chart
3. Flashcards showing family relationships
4. Pictures of grandparents, uncles, aunts, and cousins
5. Charts showing family members and their obligations
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
A family is made up of people who are related by blood, marriage, or adoption. Apart from parents and children, there are other people who are important members of the family, such as grandparents, uncles, aunts, cousins, nephews, and nieces.
Family members have different relationships with one another and also have responsibilities towards the family. When family members love, respect, help, and cooperate with one another, the family becomes peaceful and united.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about other people in the family, their relationships with us, and the obligations of different family members.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF FAMILY MEMBERS
Family members are people who are related to one another by blood, marriage, or adoption. Apart from parents and children, there are other people who are important members of a family.
OTHER FAMILY MEMBERS AND THEIR RELATIONSHIPS
1. Grandfather - the father of one’s father or mother.
2. Grandmother - the mother of one’s father or mother.
3. Uncle - the brother of one’s father or mother.
4. Aunt - the sister of one’s father or mother.
5. Cousin - the child of one’s uncle or aunt.
6. Nephew - the son of one’s brother or sister.
7. Niece - the daughter of one’s brother or sister.
8. Brother - a male child of the same parents.
9. Sister - a female child of the same parents.
LESSON 2 - OBLIGATIONS OF FAMILY MEMBERS
Every family member has responsibilities that help the family live peacefully and successfully.
OBLIGATIONS of PARENTS AND GUARDIANS
Parents and guardians:
1. Provide food, clothing, and shelter.
2. Pay children’s school fees and provide learning materials.
3. Provide healthcare and protection.
4. Teach children good behaviour and values.
5. Guide and discipline children appropriately.
OBLIGATIONS OF CHILDREN
Children:
1. Respect parents, guardians, and older family members.
2. Obey reasonable family rules.
3. Help with household chores.
4. Study hard and take education seriously.
5. Care for younger family members.
6. Protect family property.
7. Show love and kindness to other family members.
LESSON 3 - OBLIGATIONS OF OTHER FAMILY MEMBERS
Grandparents, uncles, aunts, cousins, and other relatives should:
1. Show love and care for one another.
2. Support family members when necessary.
3. Respect one another.
4. Help settle disagreements peacefully.
5. Encourage good behaviour.
6. Assist children in their education and development where possible.
IMPORTANCE OF FAMILY OBLIGATIONS
Family obligations are important because they:
1. Promote love and unity.
2. Encourage peaceful living.
3. Create cooperation among family members.
4. Teach children responsibility and respect.
5. Help family members support one another.
6. Make the family a safe and happy place to live.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. The father of one’s father or mother is called a ______.
A. grandfather
B. uncle
C. cousin
D. nephew
2. The sister of one’s father or mother is called an ______.
A. niece
B. aunt
C. grandmother
D. cousin
3. The child of one’s uncle or aunt is one’s ______.
A. cousin
B. nephew
C. grandfather
D. parent
4. Which of the following is an obligation of children in the family?
A. Damaging family property
B. Disobeying parents
C. Helping with household chores
D. Fighting with family members
5. Which of the following helps to promote peace in the family?
A. Selfishness
B. Quarrelling
C. Disrespect
D. Cooperation
B. Fill in the Gaps
Use the following words to complete the sentences: cousin, grandmother, chores, cousin, respect
6. The mother of one’s father or mother is one’s ______.
7. The brother of one’s father or mother is one’s ______.
8. The child of one’s uncle or aunt is one’s ______.
9. Children should show ______ to their parents and older family members.
10. Children should help with household ______.
C. True or False
11. A grandfather is the father of one’s father or mother. ______
12. An aunt is the brother of one’s parent. ______
13. Family members should love and support one another. ______
14. Children should help with appropriate household duties. ______
15. Disrespect and fighting promote peace in the family. ______
D. Matching
Match Column A with the correct answer in Column B.
16. Grandfather - A. Daughter of one’s brother or sister
17. Aunt - B. Son of one’s brother or sister
18. Cousin - C. Father of one’s father or mother
19. Nephew - D. Sister of one’s father or mother
20. Niece - E. Child of one’s uncle or aunt
ANSWER KEY
1. A 2. B 3. A 4. C 5. D
6. grandmother
7. uncle
8. cousin
9. respect
10. chores
11. True
12. False
13. True
14. True
15. False
16. C - Father of one’s father or mother
17. D - Sister of one’s father or mother
18. E - Child of one’s uncle or aunt
19. B - Son of one’s brother or sister
20. A - Daughter of one’s brother or sister
SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that family members are people related to one another by blood, marriage, or adoption. They identified other people in the family apart from parents and children, such as grandparents, uncles, aunts, cousins, nephews, and nieces.
Pupils also learned the relationships between these family members and themselves. They learned that every family member has obligations, such as showing love and respect, helping with household duties, supporting one another, obeying reasonable family rules, and protecting family property.
Family obligations promote love, unity, cooperation, peace, and responsibility among family members.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher displays a family tree chart or pictures of different family members and asks pupils:
- Who are the members of your family?
- Apart from your parents, brothers, and sisters, who else is related to you?
- What do you call your mother’s sister?
- What do you call your father’s father?
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the pictures and answer the questions.
Step 2: Meaning of Other Family Members
The teacher explains that other family members are relatives who are part of our wider or extended family apart from our parents and siblings.
- Examples include grandparents, uncles, aunts, cousins, nephews, and nieces.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention other family members they know.
Step 3: Grandparents
The teacher explains that:
- A grandfather is the father of one’s father or mother.
- A grandmother is the mother of one’s father or mother.
- Grandparents often provide love, advice, care, guidance, and family history.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify their grandparents and state ways they can show them respect.
Step 4: Uncles and Aunts
The teacher explains that:
- An uncle is the brother of one’s father or mother.
- An aunt is the sister of one’s father or mother.
- Uncles and aunts may help to guide, care for, support, and encourage younger family members.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify an uncle or aunt and explain their relationship.
Step 5: Cousins
The teacher explains that a cousin is the child of one’s uncle or aunt.
Cousins are relatives who may grow, learn, play, and participate in family activities together.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils state who their cousins are and mention activities they can do together peacefully.
Step 6: Nephews and Nieces
The teacher explains that:
- A nephew is the son of one’s brother or sister.
- A niece is the daughter of one’s brother or sister.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify the correct relationship between nephews, nieces, and themselves.
Step 7: Obligations of Parents and Guardians
The teacher explains that parents and guardians have responsibilities such as:
- Providing food, clothing, and shelter.
- Providing education and learning materials.
- Providing healthcare and protection.
- Teaching children good values.
- Guiding and correcting children appropriately.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention ways parents and guardians care for them.
Step 8: Obligations of Children
The teacher explains that children should:
- Respect parents, guardians, and older family members.
- Obey reasonable family rules.
- Help with household chores.
- Study hard.
- Care for younger family members.
- Protect family property.
- Show love and kindness to relatives.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention household duties they can perform.
Step 9: Obligations of Other Family Members
The teacher explains that grandparents, uncles, aunts, and other relatives should:
- Show love and care.
- Support family members when necessary.
- Respect one another.
- Give good advice and guidance.
- Help settle disagreements peacefully.
- Encourage children to behave well.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss how relatives can support one another.
Step 10: Importance of Family Obligations
The teacher explains that carrying out family obligations helps to:
- Promote love and unity.
- Encourage cooperation.
- Maintain peace.
- Teach children responsibility.
- Build respect among family members.
- Make the family a happy and supportive place.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention ways they can help to promote peace and unity at home.
Step 11: Group Activity
The teacher divides pupils into groups.
- Group 1: List five other family members and their relationships.
- Group 2: State five obligations of children.
- Group 3: State five obligations of parents and guardians.
- Group 4: Explain why family members should love, respect, and support one another.
Each group presents its work.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write, and present their answers.
Step 12: Lesson Summary
The teacher reviews the other people in the family, their relationships, and the obligations of different family members.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 13: Evaluation
The teacher gives pupils the 20-question practice exercise.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils complete the Multiple Choice, Fill in the Gaps, True or False, and Matching questions.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Unity in Cultural Diversity: Meaning of Cultural Diversity and Unity, Culture as a People’s Way of Life, Customs, Traditions and Changeable Customs | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 2 Social Studies
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils to,
1. Explain the meaning of family members.
2. Mention at least six other people in the family apart from parents and children.
3. Explain the relationship between grandparents, uncles, aunts, cousins, nephews, and nieces and themselves.
4. State at least five obligations of family members.
5. Mention at least three obligations of children in the family.
6. Explain how love, respect, cooperation, and responsibility promote peace and unity in the family.
